featured_videos.title: What I Eat in a Day as a Carnivore Doctor
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: What I Eat in a Day as a Carnivore Doctor
featured_videos.commentary: The community's eating this up, and honestly, it's because Dr. Hampton keeps it real simple. What's hitting hardest in the comments? People are talking about *systems*, not perfection. Burger bowls, make-enough-for-tomorrow lunches, baked egg batches on Sunday, slow cooker roasts that last six meals. This isn't complicated macro tracking or exotic ingredient hunting, it's just "I made this once and now I eat it five times." That's what actually sticks for people who are busy, traveling, or just tired of thinking about food. The comment from the guy in Europe living on eggs and sardines for under three euros a day? That's the real story here. He solved for simplicity, budget, and his IBS in one move. That's what works when you stop chasing the perfect plate and start solving for your actual life.

featured_videos.title: the ULTIMATE Carnivore comfort breakfast
featured_videos.creator: Courtney Luna
featured_videos.commentary: What's great about this video is that Courtney's showing something most people overlook: comfort food doesn't have to disappear on carnivore. Biscuits and gravy feels nostalgic and deeply satisfying, which matters because sustainability isn't about white-knuckling through meals you hate. The community's loving it too, and honestly, the fact that she lost 9 pounds in her first month doing carnivore OMAD while still enjoying breakfast like this tells you everything you need to know. Real food, real results, real life, apron or no apron.

featured_videos.title: Please Give Me 5 Minutes 🙏
featured_videos.creator: No Carb Life
featured_videos.commentary: The comments are telling the real story here, and it's not about the diet itself. It's about what happens when people actually *commit* instead of negotiate. That top comment about the nephew who lost weight, gained it back after quitting, then somehow proved carnivore works by failing to follow it? That's the conversation happening in a thousand family dinners right now. People want the magic pill without the non-negotiable part. The ones sharing their wins, like the 37-year-old who reversed her autoimmune symptoms or the retired LEO who finally broke free after decades, they all say the same thing: no exceptions, no compromise. That's not sexy or easy to sell, but it's what actually works. Dave's asking for stories because the stories are the proof that nobody can argue with.

featured_videos.title: Dr. Mike Thinks Carnivore Is a Bad Idea. Here's What He Missed
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.editorial_title: Dr. Mike Thinks Carnivore Is a Bad Idea. Here's What He Missed
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here tell the real story. People are off medications, their digestion improved, gout disappeared. Meanwhile the criticism boils down to "but where's your fiber?" It's the same fiber argument we've heard for years, and it keeps losing to actual results. What matters most is that carnivore is working for thousands of people who tried everything else first, and that's something worth paying attention to instead of dismissing based on nutrition dogma from 1985.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore.. Heading back to the ER.  Part 1
featured_videos.creator: Bill and Daisy Alaska
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore Heading back to the ER.  Part 1
featured_videos.commentary: Bill's honesty about stepping back when life gets complicated is something the carnivore community needs to hear more often. Too many people treat the diet like a rigid protocol that can't bend, but real health is messy. it includes doctor visits, family stress, and sometimes just taking a break to handle what matters. The fact that he's still committed to carnivore nearly three years in while navigating whatever's in this video tells you something: protocol beats perfection, but life beats protocol. Wishing Bill and Daisy all the best through whatever's next.

featured_videos.title: This Keto Salad Will Upset the Carnivore Police
featured_videos.creator: Chris Cooking Nashville
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Keto Salad Will Upset the Carnivore Police
featured_videos.commentary: Chris nailed something important here, and the comments prove it: the carnivore community has a gatekeeping problem, and it's way worse than we admit. Someone even called it out directly. saying carnivore folks are more dogmatic than the vegans they used to be. That's a mirror we need to look in. The truth is, people thrive on different versions of this way of eating. Some do strict muscle meat. Others do what Chris is doing. adding low-carb vegetables strategically. Both work. Both are valid. What matters most isn't the label you use or whether cucumbers pass some invisible purity test, it's whether you feel better and your health markers improve. If someone wants to call themselves ketovore, dirty carnivore, or just "mostly meat with some veggies," that's their business. We should be celebrating that Chris is making food people actually want to eat, not policing his plate.
